2 April
On this day in 1757

Timur Shah (son of Ahmad Shah) and Jahan Khan (Governor of Lahore) attacked Sri Harmandir Sahib

Destroyed Sri Darbar Sahib and completely filled sarowar with debris. During the 4th invasion of Ahmad Shah in 1756-7, he reached Delhi and systematically plundered the city. But he was forced to returned back due to outbreak of cholera epidemic in his troops. During this invasion, Sirhind was annexed to his empire. Ala Singh of Patiala submitted to Ahmad Shah. But the Sikhs attacked Timur Shah at Sunam and relieved him of half of his treasure. Sikhs also attacked the rear of Afghan troops and relieved them of a lot of their loot. As a result, the infuriorated Ahmad Shah sent an expedition against the Sikhs that destroyed Sri Harimandir Sahib and filled the holy tank with debris.

2 April brings together four moments of Sikh history, from 1757 to 1984. The main event of the day is from 1757: Timur Shah (son of Ahmad Shah) and Jahan Khan (Governor of Lahore) attacked Sri Harmandir Sahib. Together they span four periods, from Persecution, the Dal Khalsa and Abdali's invasions (1717–1764) to From the Anandpur Sahib Resolution to 1984 (1967–1984). People, places and movements connected with this day include Ahmad Shah Abdali, the misl sardars, Sri Harmandir Sahib (Darbar Sahib) and Lahore.

Also on this day

  • 1809Treaty of Amritsar signed between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the British Maharaja Ranjit Singh desired to be the overlord of all Sikh States. The British gave protection to Cis-Sutlej States and confined Maharaja Ranjit Singh to Sutlej and thus came very close to Lahore. After quite a bit of sabre rattling Maharaja Ranjit Singh succumbed to British pressure. This treaty was a major defeat for Maharaja Ranjit Singh at the hands of the British. Maharaja Ranjit Singh withdrew his forces from Faridkot and Malerkotla.
  • 1850The Sikh forces of Maharaja Ranjit Singh were disbanded, approximately a year after the East Indian Company gained controled of Punjab on Mar 29, 1849.
  • 1984Harbans Lal Khana is murdered

Historical background

Persecution, the Dal Khalsa and Abdali's invasions (1717–1764)

After Banda Singh's death the Mughal governors of Lahore, notably Zakariya Khan and Mir Mannu, put prices on Sikh heads, and many Sikhs, such as Bhai Mani Singh and Bhai Taru Singh, were executed. The Sikhs organised in jathas, united as the Dal Khalsa in 1748 and resisted the repeated invasions of Ahmad Shah Abdali, who killed thousands of Sikhs in the Vadda Ghallughara of 1762 and blew up Sri Harmandir Sahib, which the Sikhs rebuilt.

On this day in this period: 1757 Timur Shah (son of Ahmad Shah) and Jahan Khan (Governor of Lahore) attacked Sri Harmandir….

The Sikh Empire of Maharaja Ranjit Singh (1799–1839)

Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia misl took Lahore in 1799, was proclaimed Maharaja in 1801 and united the misls into a single state stretching from Peshawar and Kashmir to the Sutlej. He modernised the Khalsa army, gilded Sri Harmandir Sahib, and kept peace with the British under the Treaty of Amritsar (1809).

On this day in this period: 1809 Treaty of Amritsar signed between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the British.

Colonial Punjab and the Singh Sabha revival (1850–1919)

Under British rule Sikhs were recruited in large numbers into the army while new reform movements arose: the Namdhari (Kuka) movement, the Singh Sabha movement founded at Amritsar in 1873, the Chief Khalsa Diwan (1902), Khalsa College and the Anand Marriage Act (1909). The period ended with the Ghadar movement, the Komagata Maru episode (1914) and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919.

On this day in this period: 1850 The Sikh forces of Maharaja Ranjit Singh were disbanded, approximately a year after the….

From the Anandpur Sahib Resolution to 1984 (1967–1984)

The Akali Dal adopted the Anandpur Sahib Resolution in 1973 and launched the Dharam Yudh Morcha in 1982 over river waters, Chandigarh and greater state autonomy. Tensions culminated in Operation Blue Star, the Indian Army's assault on the Darbar Sahib complex in June 1984, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on 31 October 1984 and the anti-Sikh violence in Delhi and elsewhere that followed.

On this day in this period: 1984 Harbans Lal Khana is murdered.

People and places of this day

Ahmad Shah Abdali

The founder of the Durrani Empire of Afghanistan (c. 1722–1772), who invaded India repeatedly from 1747 to 1767. His campaigns against the Sikhs included the Vadda Ghallughara of February 1762 and the destruction of Sri Harmandir Sahib, but Sikh resistance prevented him from holding Punjab.

Mentioned on 15 other days of the year

The misl sardars

The leaders of the Sikh confederacies of the 18th century, such as Nawab Kapur Singh, Jassa Singh Ahluwalia, Jassa Singh Ramgarhia, Baghel Singh and Baba Ala Singh of Patiala. Organised as the Dal Khalsa, they resisted the Afghans and in 1783 Baghel Singh's forces entered Delhi and marked the Sikh historical sites there.

Mentioned on 26 other days of the year

Sri Harmandir Sahib (Darbar Sahib)

The central Sikh shrine in Amritsar, built by Guru Arjan Dev Ji in the middle of the sacred pool, where the Adi Granth was installed in 1604. Destroyed by Ahmad Shah Abdali and rebuilt, it was covered in gold under Maharaja Ranjit Singh and has been at the centre of many events in Sikh history.

Read more → · Mentioned on 51 other days of the year

Lahore

The historic capital of Punjab, where Guru Arjan Dev Ji was martyred (Gurdwara Dera Sahib) and Maharaja Ranjit Singh ruled the Sikh Empire from the Lahore Fort. After 1947 it became part of Pakistan.

Mentioned on 62 other days of the year

Sirhind (Fatehgarh Sahib)

The Mughal provincial town where the younger Sahibzade were executed in December 1704; Gurdwara Fatehgarh Sahib marks the site. Banda Singh Bahadur captured Sirhind in 1710, and the Dal Khalsa took and razed it in 1764.

Read more → · Mentioned on 23 other days of the year

Delhi

The Mughal capital, where Guru Har Krishan Ji died (Gurdwara Bangla Sahib), Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed (Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib) and Banda Singh Bahadur was put to death in 1716. Baghel Singh's forces entered the city in 1783 and marked its Sikh sites.

Read more → · Mentioned on 52 other days of the year

Maharaja Ranjit Singh

The founder of the Sikh Empire (1780–1839). He took Lahore in 1799, was proclaimed Maharaja in 1801, unified the misls, built a modern army, and covered Sri Harmandir Sahib in gold, giving it the name Golden Temple.

Read more → · Mentioned on 35 other days of the year

Amritsar

The city founded by Guru Ram Das Ji around the sacred pool of Amritsar. As the home of Sri Harmandir Sahib and the Akal Takht it has been the spiritual and political centre of the Sikhs for four centuries.
